question: What is the KoraLink platform?
answer:
The KoraLink platform is the digital system behind the Digital Jobs for Youth in Health program in Rwanda (March 2025 to August 2029). It grew out of the IHUZO e-marketplace and works as an offline-to-online business network.
As a KoraLink Agent you use it to:
1. Order and manage your stock
2. Record sales and earn commission
3. Sell digital services such as airtime and electricity
4. Take training and earn certificates
5. Repay your startup capital (Revolving Fund)
6. Apply for job opportunities
It is funded by the Mastercard Foundation and run by The Commons Project Foundation (TCP), together with ICT Chamber and SFH.

question: Who runs and supports KoraLink, and what does each partner do?
answer:
Four main organizations are behind KoraLink:
1. Mastercard Foundation - funds the program, oversees it and receives the mandated reports.
2. The Commons Project Foundation (TCP) - delivers the program, manages the Revolving Fund, subcontracts the implementing partners and keeps the records.
3. ICT Chamber - builds, runs and maintains the platform and gives technical support.
4. Society for Family Health (SFH) Rwanda - recruits, trains, onboards and manages Agents, distributes health products and monitors results.
There may also be a Fund Manager appointed by the Mastercard Foundation to help with finance and procurement.

question: What is the goal of KoraLink?
answer: KoraLink's main aim is to advance education and relieve poverty for young people in Rwanda, especially women, by helping them become KoraLink Agents and access work opportunities. It helps youth, women and rural communities to trade, learn and earn safely using digital tools, and supports Rwanda's Smart Village and Health Digitization strategies.

question: How many jobs and agents is KoraLink aiming for?
answer:
The program targets:
- 44,000 work opportunities in total: about 14,640 direct digital jobs in health and 29,360 indirect opportunities
- 11,762 KoraLink Agents onboarded over four years
- 80% to 90% of Agents being women, and 70% working in rural areas

question: How much can a KoraLink Agent earn per month?
answer: The program target is for Agents to reach an average monthly earning of up to USD 310 through the platform by the final year of the program. The target for Year 1 is about USD 100 per month. This is a program target, not a guaranteed income - your actual earnings depend on your sales and services.

question: What is the Level A to Level F career ladder?
answer:
KoraLink is designed so Agents can grow step by step. Your progress is tracked, mentored and supported:
- Level A: survival income
- Level C: multi-service offering (you sell more kinds of products and services)
- Level F: small business employer
Your training, sales performance and ratings from employers help you move up.
keywords: how do i grow as an agent

question: What types of agents join KoraLink?
answer: Agent candidates range from Level A (no prior experience but motivated) up to Group D, which includes professionals such as nurses who can offer higher-value services.

question: What does the KoraLink platform NOT do?
answer:
The platform does not handle:
1. Physical delivery of products - SFH and other partners do the transport and logistics.
2. Medical or diagnostic services - it only enables selling health goods and services (such as telehealth subscriptions).
3. Overall budget and procurement outside its transactions - a Fund Manager may handle that.
4. Program contract management between the Foundation and TCP.
5. A dedicated CRM system and tracking of IoT devices - these are planned for later phases.

question: Who delivers my stock to me?
answer: SFH is responsible for the physical distribution of health products from its central and regional warehouses to Agents. The platform only tracks the order and delivery digitally (for example through the Dispatch Management System). You confirm the stock in the app once it is delivered.

question: Can I use KoraLink without internet?
answer:
KoraLink has an offline-friendly design for areas with weak connectivity:
- USSD/SMS: you can record sales, check earnings and fund status, make voluntary repayments, check your Outstanding Startup Capital and Monthly Installment, and place an order with the system-determined voucher.
- Sales can be recorded offline and are submitted later when you are connected.
- Training content you download works offline for 7 days, and you can draft forum replies offline (they sync later).
- Messages already delivered and downloaded help content can be read offline.
Digital service transactions (airtime, electricity, tax, TV) always need live internet and cannot be saved for later.

question: Which languages does KoraLink support?
answer: KoraLink works in Kinyarwanda and English. You can switch the app language at any time from the app settings, without logging out and without losing any work in progress. Your choice is remembered across sessions and devices. Interface text, notifications, help content, agreements, annexes and consent statements are available in both languages. If a translation is missing, the app shows the English text instead of a blank label.

question: What can my supervisor see about me?
answer: SFH supervisors and admins can see your availability status, your orders, stock, repayment status, performance score, tier and agreement status, so they can support you. They only see Agents within their assigned district or scope. You can only see your own records - other Agents cannot see your data.

question: Who can see my personal data and scores?
answer: Your own scoring data, stock, orders and commissions are visible only to you. SFH Admins can read Agent records within their assigned scope. Employers can see your professional profile (qualifications, certificates, performance metrics and ratings) when you apply for jobs. The system blocks access to other Agents' data.

question: How do I become a KoraLink Agent?
answer:
The process works like this:
1. Apply through mobile, web or USSD.
2. The system gives you a preliminary group (A, B or C) from the information on your form.
3. An SFH interviewer records your interview results and score.
4. An SFH Admin approves or rejects your application.
5. If approved, you become a KoraLink Agent and receive an SMS with your login information and training links.
6. You complete the training and sign your Agent agreement in the app.
When you register you must tick the consent boxes for processing your personal information.

question: What information does the application ask for, and how is it checked?
answer: The application form collects indicators such as your income situation, disability and digital access. These are scored to assess need and readiness. During recruitment, KoraLink can also cross-check claimed income against digital income history through data agreements with MoMo, MTN and Equity. Your information is stored securely under Rwanda's data protection law.

question: How will I know if my application was approved or rejected?
answer: You are told by SMS. If you are approved, the SMS contains your login information and training details and your role is upgraded to KoraLink Agent. If you are rejected, the SMS includes the reason. If you do not understand the reason, ask your SFH supervisor or contact support.

question: What are application groups A, B and C?
answer: When you apply, the system assigns a preliminary vulnerability group (A, B or C) from the need indicators on your form, such as income, disability and technology access. It is used to support inclusive recruitment, and the final decision still comes from the interview and SFH's approval.

question: How is my agent profile created?
answer: Your profile is created automatically from data verified by SFH (your name, ID and training), so you do not have to type it in. The required fields are your SFH ID, assigned location and certifications. You can edit your personal information and upload certificates. Employers can see your profile and ratings when you apply for jobs.

question: How do I log in for the first time as an Agent?
answer: You register using your login credentials. Your SFH ID is validated automatically through the system, so you do not need extra steps. You will receive your login details by SMS after your application is approved. Your wallet needs a 4-digit PIN the first time you open it. If you cannot log in, contact your SFH supervisor or the support line.

question: What is shown on my professional profile?
answer: Your profile shows your qualifications, certificates and performance metrics such as sales volume, commission history and repayment rates, plus reputation ratings from employers. It helps employers and administrators trust your work and helps you get job opportunities. Your signed agreement and ID are also available so you can prove your status in your community.

question: Why do I have to accept consent boxes when I register?
answer: Rwanda's Law No. 058/2021 requires your informed consent before your personal information is processed. KoraLink therefore shows mandatory consent checkboxes in all registration flows. You also have rights over your data, including the right to access it and to request its erasure (some financial records must be kept for 10 years by law).

question: How do customers register on KoraLink?
answer: Customers sign up with just their phone number. A one-time code (OTP) is sent to the phone by SMS to confirm it, so they can start browsing products straight away. They can browse, order and pay digitally, and receive order confirmations.

question: What is the Agent agreement and why do I need to sign it?
answer: The Agent agreement is the legally binding Repayable Grant agreement between you and the program. It sets the terms for the startup goods, devices, digital float and data you receive and how you repay them. You must sign it digitally in the app before the Revolving Fund can be activated for you. Every voucher and every repayment you make is linked back to this signed agreement.

question: How do I sign my KoraLink agreement step by step?
answer:
Open your agreement in the app (unsigned ones are listed as awaiting signature) and read the agreement and its annexes first - they stay visible above the steps. Then complete the 7 steps in order:
1. Identity: enter your national ID number; it is checked against your SFH-verified record.
2. Phone: confirm your phone number and enter the 6-digit code sent by SMS (you can resend or use another number).
3. Consent: confirm three statements - you read the agreement, understand your obligations and accept the terms.
4. Signature: draw your signature on the screen (you can clear and redo it).
5. Biometrics: confirm with your phone's fingerprint or face unlock.
6. Liveness: take two face photos following the on-screen guide, review them, and confirm or retake.
7. Signing: confirm the information is correct, agree to sign digitally and sign.
The Continue button stays disabled until each step is valid.

question: What should I prepare before signing my agreement?
answer:
Have these ready:
- Your national ID number
- The phone number registered to your account, with network so you can receive the SMS code
- A steady internet connection
- A phone with fingerprint or face unlock if you have one
- A working camera and good, even light for the face photos
Take time to read the agreement and annexes first. Note the signing deadline and reference number shown before you open the document.

question: What if my phone has no fingerprint, face unlock or camera?
answer: For the biometrics step (step 5) and the liveness step (step 6), the system provides a recorded skip path when your device has no enrolled biometric or no camera. The use of a skip path is recorded on your signing record. All other steps cannot be skipped.

question: Can I refuse to sign the agreement?
answer: Yes. At the final step there is a Decline action, shown differently from the Sign button. If you decline, the refusal is recorded with a timestamp, your supervisor is notified and your account is not activated for Revolving Fund disbursement.

question: What happens if I miss the signing deadline?
answer: The system does not allow signing after the deadline. Expired agreements are escalated to SFH so the agreement can be reissued. SFH can see which agreements are close to their deadline and can send you reminders, so check your messages and sign before the date shown.

question: What if my signing is interrupted by network loss?
answer: A partly completed signing can be recovered without losing the steps you already finished, so you do not have to start from the beginning. Open the agreement again and continue from where you stopped.

question: Where can I find my signed agreement?
answer: Go to Profile > Agreements (Amasezerano). After you sign, the agreement moves out of the 'awaiting signature' list. The signed screen shows the signing date and time, approval date and time, your district and the agreement reference number. You can view it on screen or download it as a PDF. It stays available in your profile for as long as your account exists.

question: Can the agreement be changed after I sign it?
answer: No. Once signed, the agreement and its evidence cannot be altered. If something has to change, a new agreement version is issued with its own reference number and you go through the signing steps again.

question: When does my 18-month repayment period start?
answer: Your 18-month repayment contract starts on the date and time you sign your agreement. The platform counts the months remaining from that moment to calculate your Monthly Installment.

question: What information is stored when I sign my agreement?
answer: The signing record stores the national ID used, your verified phone number, your consent statements with timestamps, your signature image, the biometric result, the liveness photos, device and session details and your IP address. It is kept for 10 years with the signed document. Your phone's fingerprint or face template never leaves your phone - only the success or failure result is stored, and face photos are encrypted.

question: How do I order stock step by step?
answer:
1. Open the Inventory tab and tap Request Product.
2. Choose the merchant you want to order from (SFH Rwanda, Basil Industries Ltd or Land Husbandry and Agri Production (LHAP) Ltd).
3. Pick the products and set the quantity - quantities are in cases, and the app shows the number of units.
4. Select the warehouse that will fulfil the order. The app checks live whether it has enough stock.
5. Review the price breakdown: how much is covered by your voucher and how much you pay from your wallet.
6. Add an optional comment, then submit.
7. SFH reviews the order (if it includes a voucher, the voucher is approved first), the stock is reserved and delivered, and once delivery is confirmed it becomes active in your inventory.

question: Can I order from more than one merchant in the same order?
answer: No. Each order is placed with exactly one merchant, and products from different merchants cannot be combined in a single order. To stock from several suppliers, place a separate order for each merchant. Each merchant has its own catalog, prices and warehouses. Access to a merchant can be given by district or to individual Agents.

question: What does 'units per case' mean when I order?
answer: Products are ordered in cases, and each product has a fixed number of units per case - for example 200 units for envelopes, 50 for toilet paper and 12 for serviettes. The app shows how many units are in a case before you choose the quantity, and the order summary and delivery note show both cases and units. This stops you ordering part-cases that cannot be delivered, so check the units before ordering so you do not order more than you can sell.
keywords: how many units in a box

question: What does the availability warning mean on my order?
answer: It means the warehouse you selected does not have enough of that product for the quantity you asked for. The order line shows the quantity you requested next to the quantity available. You cannot submit until every warning is cleared, so either lower the quantity, remove the item or choose another warehouse (the app re-checks every line when you change warehouse). Stock that is already reserved for other orders is not counted as available.

question: What do the stock order statuses mean?
answer:
Your stock orders can show these statuses:
- Submitted: your order has been sent
- Awaiting voucher approval: SFH is reviewing the voucher on your order
- Approved: SFH accepted it and stock is being reserved
- Rejected: it was not accepted (you receive an SMS with the reason if a voucher was refused)
- Dispatched: the stock is on its way
- Delivered: the merchant confirmed delivery
- Cancelled: the order was not completed

question: How do I track my stock order?
answer: Open the stock orders view (My Requests under Inventory). It lists every order with the merchant, products and quantities, order value, submission date and current status, so you can see when to expect delivery. Any comment you added when ordering is kept on the order record.

question: Can I add a note to my stock order?
answer: Yes. You can type an optional comment when you place the order, for example special delivery instructions. It is passed to the merchant and kept on the order record.

question: When does delivered stock show in my inventory?
answer: New stock becomes active in your digital inventory only after the merchant confirms that it was physically delivered. You are also notified when administrators assign stock to you. Once the stock is active, each sale you record reduces it automatically in real time.

question: Will I be alerted when my stock is low?
answer: Yes. When your stock of a product falls below 5 units you receive an SMS, for example: 'Low stock! Only 3 nets left. Reply RESTOCK to request more'. SFH admins are also alerted when stock drops under their set limits.

question: Can I order stock without a smartphone?
answer: Yes. If you have a basic phone, you can place an order through the USSD shortcode. The system works out your voucher allocation for you, just like in the app.

question: Why was my order with a voucher cancelled or rejected?
answer: When an order includes a voucher, SFH reviews the voucher first and the order second - they are one decision. If the voucher is not approved, the order is cancelled and you receive an SMS with the reason. Contact your SFH supervisor to understand the reason and to fix it, for example if it relates to your repayment status or your agreement.

question: Who can see my stock, orders and commissions?
answer: Only you can see your own stock, orders and commissions. Access permissions limit Agents to their own records. SFH admins can view Agent data within their assigned scope. Every stock movement is saved in a permanent audit trail (source, destination, who started it, status and quantity) for 10 years.

question: How do I record a sale step by step?
answer:
1. On the Home screen tap Record Sale.
2. Choose the buyer type: Customer (an individual) or Business (shop, clinic, organization). This must be chosen first because it sets the price.
3. Tap Add Product, pick the product and set the quantity and selling price. Repeat to add more products to the same sale.
4. Choose the payment method and add notes if you want.
5. Enter the customer's name and phone number (the +250 country code is already filled in). Email is optional.
6. Check the summary - the total amount and your estimated profit update live.
7. Tap Record Sale to submit.
Your stock reduces immediately, the sale is credited to your storefront, the invoice is sent to RRA EBM, and your earnings and capital update. Always record the sale before the customer leaves.

question: What is the difference between a Customer sale and a Business sale?
answer: Choose Customer when selling to an individual and Business when selling to an institution such as a shop, clinic or organization. Each product can have a different price for each buyer type, so the correct selling price loads automatically. If you change the buyer type after adding products, the basket is re-priced and your estimated profit is recalculated. Your profit is always worked out against the same cost price.

question: How is my earning on a sale calculated?
answer: For physical products, your earning is the margin: (selling price - cost price) x quantity. Example: you sell one unit at RWF 1,433 and its cost price is RWF 550, so you earn RWF 883. Tap any sale record to see the full calculation (quantity, selling price per unit, cost price per unit and profit). For digital services your earning is a commission paid by the provider instead.

question: Can I change the selling price when recording a sale?
answer: Where price changes are allowed, you can adjust the price within the minimum and maximum limits set for that product and buyer type. You cannot record a sale at or below the cost price without authorization. If the app refuses your price, it is outside the allowed range.

question: What details are saved with every sale?
answer: Each sale record keeps: buyer type, each product with selling price, cost price and quantity, payment method, optional notes, customer name, customer phone number with country code, optional email, estimated profit, total amount, date and time, and the Agent who recorded it. You cannot submit until at least one product and all required fields are filled.
keywords: what is saved in a sale

question: Why do I have to enter the customer's name and phone number?
answer: The customer details let you find the transaction later if the customer returns, help settle disputes, and are used for the customer's SMS receipt and for the tax invoice sent to RRA. Name and phone number are required on every sale.

question: How do I look up my past sales?
answer: On the Home screen tap View Sales History. You will see your number of sales, total revenue and total earnings for the period, followed by each sale with product, date and time, amount, profit, quantity, selling price per unit and cost price per unit. You can search by product, customer name or phone number. These figures match your earnings and capital dashboards.

question: Can I record a sale when I am offline?
answer: Yes. Sale recording is available offline and is submitted later when you are connected again. If you have a basic phone you can also record sales and check earnings through USSD. Remember that digital services (airtime, electricity, tax, TV) cannot be done offline.

question: How can my customer pay me?
answer: Customers can pay by mobile money through USSD, STK push or QR code, supported by MVEND. The customer gets a payment confirmation straight away, so you can see the payment went through before you hand over the goods.

question: What does the RRA or EBM status on my sale mean?
answer: Every sale invoice is automatically sent to the Rwanda Revenue Authority's EBM e-invoice system. The sale record shows its status: Submitted (accepted by RRA), Queued under VSDC fallback (waiting to be sent), or Failed. If the network is down, the invoice is saved and retried as soon as connectivity returns. Failed submissions are logged for retry or escalation, and your supervisor can also see sales that have not reached RRA.

question: What do Total Earnings, Tax Deductions and Net Income mean?
answer:
Your earnings view shows:
- Total Earnings: your gross earnings from product margins and digital service commissions before deductions
- Tax Deductions: VAT deducted, with the applicable rate displayed
- Net Income: Total Earnings minus Tax Deductions - this is your headline earnings
Commission from digital services is also split into instant and delayed parts. Every figure can be traced to its underlying transactions.

question: Why does my VAT rate show 0%?
answer: The VAT rate is always displayed, even when it is zero. This is so that you can tell a real 0% rate apart from a calculation that is missing. If you see 0%, the tax rate applied to your earnings is zero.

question: What is Capital on my home screen?
answer:
Capital is your total business position. It includes:
- Your stock, split between physical products and digital services float
- Your accumulated earnings, split between product sales and digital services
The split between physical and digital is also used for program reporting, and every figure can be traced to its transactions.

question: What do I do if my earnings or capital figures look wrong?
answer:
1. Refresh the screen and check your internet connection.
2. Open your sales history and tap the sale to see its full calculation.
3. Check that every sale was recorded before the customer left and that its stock quantity is correct.
4. If the difference remains, note the date, product and amount and contact your SFH supervisor or support (+250 796 602 807, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00).

question: What is a voucher in KoraLink?
answer: A voucher is startup capital that the Revolving Fund gives you when you place a stock order, so you can restock without paying the full amount yourself. It is a Repayable Grant: you repay exactly what you received, with no interest. You do not ask for vouchers separately - the system works out your voucher amount automatically when you place an order, based on your phase, your voucher history and the order value.

question: Is the voucher a loan? Do I pay interest?
answer: The voucher is a Repayable Grant, not a loan. There is no interest: you repay exactly the amount you received (your Total Voucher Received), not the maximum ceiling. You repay through monthly installments, voluntary repayments and, in the Interim and Final phases, a required repayment on certain orders.

question: How do vouchers work when I place an order?
answer:
When you place an order the system does these checks for you:
1. It checks that every product in the order accepts voucher payment.
2. It uses any unused voucher balance first.
3. It finds your current phase (Initial, Interim or Final) and checks if you can move to the next one.
4. In the Interim and Final phases it asks for a required repayment from your wallet before issuing a new voucher.
5. It issues a new voucher, within your phase ceiling, the per-order limit and your remaining capacity.
6. You pay the rest of the order from your wallet.
7. Your Monthly Installment is recalculated.
The order summary shows Unused Voucher Applied + New Voucher Issued + Wallet Payment, which must equal the order amount.

question: Can I request a voucher on its own?
answer: No. Under the current model Agents cannot request vouchers separately. A voucher is issued only when you place a stock order, and the system decides the amount. The old Recent requests section and Available to request figure were removed; the screen now shows your Voucher Capacity Remaining instead.

question: What are the three voucher phases?
answer:
Vouchers are released in three phases, and you cannot skip a phase:
1. Initial / Unrestricted: total vouchers up to RWF 120,000. No repayment condition.
2. Interim: total vouchers up to RWF 240,000 (another RWF 120,000). A required repayment of 30% applies.
3. Final: total vouchers up to RWF 360,000 (another RWF 120,000). The same 30% repayment applies.
The RWF 360,000 total is the maximum you can ever receive.

question: What is the maximum voucher I can receive?
answer: The maximum cumulative voucher for any Agent is RWF 360,000 across all phases and all orders. It is shared between physical product orders and digital service float orders (Float and Refloating). The system blocks any voucher that would take you over this ceiling. In a single order the new voucher can be at most RWF 120,000.

question: How do I move from the Initial phase to the Interim phase?
answer:
You need to meet both conditions at the same time:
1. You have consumed (used in confirmed orders) at least RWF 108,000 of vouchers - that is 90% of the RWF 120,000 Initial value.
2. At least 30 days have passed since you entered the Initial phase.
The system checks this on every order. If both are met, you move up at your next order and receive an SMS confirming your new voucher capacity.

question: How do I move from the Interim phase to the Final phase?
answer:
Again you need both conditions together:
1. You have consumed at least RWF 216,000 of vouchers in total (90% of RWF 240,000).
2. At least 30 days have passed since you entered the Interim phase.
If only one condition is met nothing changes. Once both are met you move to Final at your next order and receive an SMS.

question: Why am I still in the same phase when I reached my ceiling?
answer: Reaching a phase's voucher ceiling does not move you to the next phase. You move only when you have consumed 90% of the cumulative value AND 30 days have passed since you entered the current phase. Also, repaying money does not create extra voucher capacity - capacity only grows through phase changes. Check your dashboard to see your consumed amount against the next threshold and the days passed.

question: How can I see my phase progress?
answer: Your dashboard shows your current phase, how much voucher you have consumed against the next threshold, and how many days have passed since your current phase started (against the 30-day requirement). When you move to a new phase you get an SMS and the dashboard updates immediately with your new Voucher Capacity Remaining.
keywords: how close am i to next phase

question: What is the required repayment in the Interim and Final phases?
answer: Before a new voucher is issued in the Interim or Final phase, the wallet part of your order must cover a required repayment equal to the smaller of 30% of your Outstanding Startup Capital and the remaining order amount. This money is paid from your wallet as part of the order and counts as repayment, so it reduces what you owe. This rule does not apply in the Initial phase.

question: What if my wallet does not have enough for the required repayment?
answer: The system will not issue a new voucher and will block the order, showing a message with the minimum wallet balance needed. Top up your wallet and place the order again. In Initial phase this condition does not apply.

question: Can you show an example of an order in the Initial phase?
answer:
Example (for illustration): you are in the Initial phase, your Total Voucher Received is RWF 60,000 and you have RWF 10,000 unused voucher. You order RWF 150,000.
1. Unused voucher applied: RWF 10,000, leaving RWF 140,000.
2. Phase ceiling remaining: 120,000 - 60,000 = RWF 60,000.
3. New voucher = the smallest of 140,000 (order left), 120,000 (per-order cap), 60,000 (phase ceiling left) and your remaining capacity = RWF 60,000.
4. Wallet payment = 150,000 - 10,000 - 60,000 = RWF 80,000.
Check: 10,000 + 60,000 + 80,000 = 150,000.
keywords: how much will i pay example

question: Can you show an example of an order in the Interim phase?
answer:
Example (for illustration): you are in the Interim phase, Outstanding Startup Capital is RWF 200,000, Total Voucher Received is RWF 220,000, no unused voucher, and you order RWF 100,000.
1. Required repayment = smaller of 30% x 200,000 = 60,000 and the order (100,000) = RWF 60,000.
2. Order left after repayment = RWF 40,000.
3. Phase ceiling remaining = 240,000 - 220,000 = RWF 20,000.
4. New voucher = smallest of 40,000, 120,000, 20,000 and your remaining capacity = RWF 20,000.
5. Wallet payment = 100,000 - 0 - 20,000 = RWF 80,000, of which RWF 60,000 counts as repayment.

question: What does my order summary show for voucher and payment?
answer: The summary shows your current phase, Total Voucher Received, Unused Voucher Balance and Voucher Capacity Remaining, then the payment breakdown: Unused Voucher Applied, New Voucher Issued and Wallet Payment (and the Required Repayment in Interim and Final phases). The system confirms that these add up to the order amount before the order is submitted. If they do not match, the order is stopped and flagged for investigation.

question: Is my unused voucher used before a new one is issued?
answer: Yes. Any unused voucher balance must be fully applied to your order before the system issues a new voucher. If the unused balance already covers the whole order, no new voucher is issued.

question: What if one product in my order does not accept vouchers?
answer: Then no voucher is used on that order at all: the whole order is paid from your wallet. Vouchers cannot be applied to part of a mixed order. If you want to use your voucher, order the voucher-eligible products in a separate order.

question: Can I use vouchers for digital service float?
answer: Yes. Float and refloating orders follow the same three-phase voucher rules as physical products, and count toward the same RWF 360,000 total. The system first checks if the digital service provider accepts voucher payment; if it does not, you pay the full amount from your wallet. The same payment breakdown is shown.

question: What do Total Voucher Received, Unused Voucher Balance and Outstanding Startup Capital mean?
answer:
- Total Voucher Received: everything issued to you in all orders. It never goes down.
- Cumulative Voucher Consumed: the vouchers actually applied to confirmed orders. It is used for phase progress.
- Unused Voucher Balance: voucher received but not yet used in an order.
- Outstanding Startup Capital: what you still owe = Total Voucher Received - Total Confirmed Repayments (never below zero).
- Voucher Capacity Remaining: 360,000 - Total Voucher Received.
- Phase Ceiling: 120,000 (Initial), 240,000 (Interim) or 360,000 (Final).

question: What does my voucher screen show?
answer: Your voucher screen shows your current phase, Unused Voucher Balance, Phase Ceiling, Maximum Allowed Voucher (RWF 360,000) and Voucher Capacity Remaining. Below, each voucher is listed with its reference, total value, remaining value, expiry date where it applies and status (partially used, fully used or expired). You can copy a voucher reference to give to support. The same balance figures appear at checkout. If you have a special limit set for you personally, the screen says so.

question: Is there a 4% charge on my wallet payments?
answer: No. Under the current model no percentage is added to or deducted from your wallet payments. Startup capital is recovered only through your scheduled monthly installments, any voluntary repayments you make, and the required repayment on Interim and Final phase orders. (Earlier program versions used a 4% deduction on wallet orders; that is no longer part of the model.)

question: What is my Monthly Installment and how is it worked out?
answer:
Your Monthly Installment is what you are scheduled to repay each month:
Monthly Installment = Outstanding Startup Capital / Remaining Repayment Periods (months left on your 18-month contract).
Example: you used RWF 240,000 and repaid RWF 60,000, so you owe RWF 180,000 with 8 months left: installment = RWF 22,500. It is recalculated automatically whenever your balance or months remaining change, and you can see it on your Wallet dashboard together with the next due date.
keywords: how much do i pay monthly

question: Why did my monthly installment go up?
answer: The installment is recalculated whenever something changes. It goes up when you receive a new voucher, because your Outstanding Startup Capital rises. Also, because your contract is fixed at 18 months, capital used later is repaid over fewer months: capital drawn in month 12 is repaid over the 6 remaining months, giving a higher installment than the same amount drawn in month 2. Example: owing RWF 180,000 over 8 months is RWF 22,500; after using RWF 60,000 more you owe 240,000 and the installment becomes RWF 30,000.

question: How can I lower my monthly installment?
answer: Repay some of your balance early. Any successful repayment reduces your Outstanding Startup Capital and the installment is recalculated immediately. Example: with RWF 180,000 owed and 8 months left, a voluntary repayment of RWF 60,000 leaves RWF 120,000 and your installment drops to RWF 15,000.

question: How do I make a voluntary repayment in the app?
answer:
1. Open the Wallet section.
2. Choose Make Repayment.
3. Enter the amount - anything from RWF 1 up to your full Outstanding Startup Capital.
4. Confirm with your PIN.
The payment is processed through MVEND in real time, your balance and installment update immediately, and the progress bar moves. You then receive an SMS: 'RWF [Amount] received. Your outstanding balance is now RWF [New Balance]. Your new monthly installment is RWF [New Installment].'

question: How do I make a repayment using USSD?
answer: If you have a basic phone, dial the repayment USSD shortcode, choose the repayment menu (it shows your current Outstanding Startup Capital), enter the amount and confirm. You receive an SMS confirmation. You can also check your Outstanding Startup Capital and Monthly Installment by USSD.

question: Can I repay more than I owe?
answer: No. A repayment cannot be more than your Outstanding Startup Capital. If you try, the payment is rejected and the app tells you the maximum amount you can pay. Your balance can never go below zero.

question: What are Paid and Pending repayments?
answer: The repayment ledger lists every repayment (scheduled installment, voluntary repayment or order repayment) with date and time, type, source reference, amount and state, newest first. Paid means the payment has settled. Pending means it is still being processed. Only Paid amounts count in your Total Confirmed Repayments and progress bar, and the screen says that pending amounts are not yet included. If a payment stays pending for long, contact support - SFH monitors old pending payments.

question: How long do I have to repay my startup capital?
answer: You repay over an 18-month contract that begins on the day you sign your agreement. The repayment is interest-free, and based only on the capital you actually used. Once your Outstanding Startup Capital reaches zero, your obligation is marked Fully Repaid and no more installments are due.

question: What happens if I still owe money after 18 months?
answer: If a balance remains at the end of the 18-month term, the platform flags your record, stops recalculating your installment and keeps the remaining balance on your record. The program collects it outside the current collection system, and any repayments you still make are recorded against it. Speak to your SFH supervisor before the end of your term if you think you will have a balance.

question: What if I cannot afford my installment?
answer: Talk to your SFH supervisor as early as possible. SFH admins have tools to filter Agents who are behind, to manage hardship cases and to authorize partial payments, and they can send reminders. You can also pay in smaller amounts: voluntary repayments can be any amount from RWF 1. Each payment you make reduces what you owe.

question: How do I check how much I still owe?
answer: Open your Wallet dashboard. It shows Total Voucher Received, Total Confirmed Repayments, Outstanding Startup Capital, your current Monthly Installment, months remaining on your contract, the next installment due date and a repayment progress bar. When the balance reaches zero it shows Fully Repaid.

question: What do On Track, Overdue and Fully Repaid mean?
answer: These are repayment statuses SFH sees for each Agent: On Track means your installments are paid as scheduled, Overdue means an installment is late, and Fully Repaid means your Outstanding Startup Capital is zero. SFH can filter Agents by overdue status to give support and can send reminders in bulk.

question: What happens to vouchers I already received before the new voucher model?
answer: Nothing is reset. If you were active before the new model started, you are placed in a starting phase based on your historical Total Voucher Received: less than RWF 120,000 = Initial; RWF 120,000 to below 240,000 = Interim; RWF 240,000 or more = Final. Your history and phase dates are kept.

question: How is float I received earlier through DDIN counted?
answer: Digital service float you previously got through DDIN is loaded once as your opening Total Voucher Received. It decides your starting phase and is counted in your Outstanding Startup Capital. SFH can see this opening balance separately from vouchers issued through marketplace orders.

question: Does repaying give me more voucher capacity?
answer: No. Repayments reduce what you owe and your monthly installment, but they do not create new voucher capacity. Your capacity only increases when you move to the next phase.

question: How does SFH approve an order that includes a voucher?
answer: SFH admins see pending voucher orders with your phase, Outstanding Startup Capital, consumption and phase status. When they approve the voucher, your order is approved at the same time and the stock is reserved. When they reject the voucher, the order is cancelled and you receive an SMS with the reason.

question: How do I see my phone repayment?
answer: Your phone repayment status is shown in your profile next to your Revolving Fund position, taken from the IntelliGra system. Your expected monthly phone repayment is 392 RWF x the days in the month. If the information cannot be retrieved, the app says it is temporarily unavailable (this is different from a zero balance) and offers a retry. If it keeps failing, report it to support.

question: How do I set up my wallet PIN?
answer:
The first time you open the Wallet, the app asks you to set a PIN:
1. Enter a 4-digit PIN (you can use the eye icon to see it).
2. Enter the same PIN again to confirm.
3. Tap the confirm button, which only works when both entries match.
Choose a PIN others cannot guess - easy patterns like 1234, 0000 or repeated digits are rejected. No wallet function (balance, payments, repayments) works until the PIN is set. Never share it.

question: What if I forget my wallet PIN?
answer: Your PIN is stored encrypted and nobody - not even a system administrator - can see it. To reset it, you must prove your identity with a one-time code sent to you. A supervisor cannot set a PIN for you. Contact support if the reset option does not work, and never tell your PIN to anyone.

question: What happens if I enter the wrong PIN several times?
answer: After several failed attempts in a row, wallet transactions are locked for a set period for your safety, and the event is recorded in the audit trail. Wait for the lock period to end and try again carefully, or use the PIN reset with a one-time code.

question: What is the Ikofi wallet used for?
answer: Ikofi is your in-app wallet, powered by MVEND. You use it to pay the wallet part of your stock orders, make repayments and handle your funds. Every financial operation needs your 4-digit PIN. You must set the PIN before you can use the wallet.

question: Which digital services can I sell?
answer:
Through the DDIN provider in the Services tab you can currently sell:
- Prepaid electricity (EUCL)
- MTN airtime
- Airtel airtime
- RRA tax payments
- Startimes PayTV subscriptions
You earn a commission on each successful transaction. The list can grow as new providers are added, and you only see the services you are authorized and certified to sell - a service that needs a certificate you do not hold is hidden or shown as locked with the certificate named.

question: How does the two-step process for digital services work?
answer:
Every digital service uses the same two steps:
Step 1 - Validate: you enter the customer's identifier (meter number, phone number, tax Doc ID or smart card number). The provider checks it and may return the account holder's name or the amount due. Read it back to the customer to confirm.
Step 2 - Execute: you confirm the amount, the system takes it from your float, sends the transaction to the provider, and shows the result with a token or receipt where relevant. Your commission is then recorded.
The Execute button stays disabled until validation succeeds, so money is not sent to a wrong account.

question: How do I sell MTN or Airtel airtime step by step?
answer:
1. Open the Services tab and select DDIN.
2. Check your Digital Services Balance at the top.
3. Tap MTN Airtime or Airtel Airtime.
4. Enter the customer's phone number and tap Validate. MTN numbers use the 78 prefix; Airtel numbers use 72 or 73.
5. After validation succeeds, enter the amount and confirm it with the customer.
6. Tap Execute. The airtime is credited to the number and your commission is recorded.
It is good practice to collect the customer's money before executing.

question: How do I sell prepaid electricity (EUCL) to a customer?
answer:
1. Open Services > DDIN > Prepaid Electricity.
2. Enter the customer's meter number (at least 8 digits) and tap Validate. Confirm the account details with the customer.
3. Enter the amount and confirm.
4. Tap Execute.
5. The electricity token appears on the screen. Give it to the customer (read it out or send it by SMS) so they can enter it on their meter. The token is saved on the transaction and can be re-sent by SMS.

question: How do I pay RRA tax for a customer?
answer:
1. Open Services > DDIN > RRA Tax.
2. Enter the declaration Doc ID and tap Validate. The provider returns the amount due.
3. Confirm the amount with the customer.
4. Tap Execute. The payment is applied to the declaration.

question: How do I renew a Startimes PayTV subscription?
answer:
1. Open Services > DDIN > Startimes PayTV.
2. Enter the customer's smart card number and tap Validate. The provider returns the subscriber.
3. Confirm the subscriber with the customer and select the package and amount.
4. Tap Execute. The subscription is extended.

question: What is my Digital Services Balance (float)?
answer: Your Digital Services Balance, also called float, is the money you use to pay providers when you sell digital services. It is shown at the top of the provider screen and refreshes after every transaction (or on demand). Each successful sale reduces it. If it is lower than the amount a customer wants, the app blocks the transaction and tells you the balance available. You top it up by placing a float (refloat) order, which can also use vouchers.

question: Why does validation fail for my customer's number?
answer: The app gives a specific reason: the format is invalid (for example a meter number under 8 digits or a phone number with the wrong prefix), the account was not found, or the provider is unavailable. Check the number with the customer and try again. If the provider is unavailable, wait and retry later.

question: What should I do if a digital service transaction fails?
answer:
1. Check the status on screen and in Services > DDIN > History.
2. A failed transaction shows whether your float was debited and, if so, whether it has been reversed. The system reconciles unclear transactions with the provider automatically.
3. Do not collect (or return) the customer's money until you know the final status.
4. Do not keep tapping Execute - each request carries a unique key so it cannot be applied twice, but you should wait for the result first.
5. If it is still not resolved, note the date, time, amount and customer number and contact support.

question: A customer says they did not receive airtime or a token. What can I do?
answer: Open Services > DDIN > History and search by customer number, date or service type. Check the record: it shows the service, number, amount, status, commission and time. If it succeeded, the provider accepted it - for a token you can re-send it to the customer by SMS. If it failed, check whether your float was reversed. If the customer is still affected, give the date, time and amount to support.

question: What is instant commission and delayed commission?
answer: For digital services you earn a commission from the provider. Instant commission is credited to you at the time of the transaction. Delayed commission is settled by the provider later. Your transaction history shows both separately and the total, and they appear in the digital services part of your earnings.

question: Can I sell digital services when I am offline?
answer: No. Digital service transactions need a live connection because the provider's price and account status must be checked at that moment. They cannot be saved for later submission, and the app tells you clearly instead of pretending to accept them. Wait until you have network, then validate and execute.

question: Why does a service show as temporarily unavailable?
answer: The provider's connection is not available right now. The app shows the service as temporarily unavailable instead of letting a transaction fail halfway. Try again later. The downtime is recorded and reported to the team.

question: Can my customer be charged twice if my network drops?
answer: No. Every execute request carries a unique key, so a retry after a timeout cannot debit your float twice or deliver the service twice. Your float is also debited and the transaction submitted as one operation, and if the provider rejects it after debit the amount is automatically reversed.

question: How do I download training for offline use?
answer: Open the training module and tap the Download icon on a video or PDF. The content is stored on your phone for 7 days so you can study without internet, for example on market days.

question: How do I earn a certificate?
answer:
1. Complete the learning modules set for your track (you can download them for offline use).
2. Pass the product information test.
3. The system issues your certificate or badge and adds it to your profile.
Certificates unlock eligibility for related services and jobs, and they show employers your skills.

question: What if I fail a quiz?
answer: After a failed quiz you get a Review Mistakes button so you can see what to improve. You can retake the quiz up to 3 times. Once you pass, your certification is issued and unlocks job eligibility.

question: What happens when my certificate expires?
answer: Certificates can expire, for example after product updates. The system automatically revokes the expired certificate, blocks the related gigs or services until you renew it and sends you an SMS asking you to retrain. Retake the training to get your certificate back.

question: Will I get reminders for training sessions?
answer: Yes. Your upcoming training sessions appear automatically in your calendar, and you get an SMS reminder 1 hour before each session.

question: Can I practice placing orders before doing it for real?
answer: Yes. Training modules include practice (sandbox) environments where you can place practice orders and try actions safely while you learn, rather than only watching videos.

question: How do I ask questions or discuss lessons with other agents?
answer: Course facilitators pin 'Concept Deep-Dive' discussion threads in training modules. You can reply from the app, write replies offline (they are sent when you reconnect), and like or upvote helpful answers from other agents. You can get SMS or push notifications when there are new topics or replies.

question: How do I give feedback on a training module?
answer: At the end of every completed module, tap the Feedback button. You can give a rating from 1 to 5 stars and write comments. You can also choose to send your feedback anonymously. SFH uses it to improve the training.

question: How is my monthly performance score calculated?
answer:
Each month your score is made of three parts:
1. Repayments (up to 20 points) - your phone repayment percentage
2. Sales (up to 50 points) - your total sales value for the month
3. Orders (up to 30 points) - the value of your paid stock orders
Your points decide your tier: Bronze, Silver, Gold or Platinum. Scoring runs automatically, normally on the first day of the following month. Your dashboard shows each score card with the numbers used and whether a minimum was missed.

question: How do I get repayment points?
answer:
Repayment points come from your phone repayment: actual repayment divided by expected repayment (expected = 392 RWF x days in the month), taken from IntelliGra:
- 100% or more: 20 points
- 90% or more: 15 points
- 80% or more: 10 points
- 70% or more: 5 points
- below 70%: 0 points
If you did not receive a smartphone through KoraLink, repayment points do not apply to you and the card is hidden.

question: How do I get sales points?
answer:
Sales points depend on your total sales value for the month (the platform uses the recommended retail price, or your higher entered price where applicable):
- below RWF 50,000: 0 points
- 50,000 to 100,000: 10 points
- 100,001 to 150,000: 20 points
- 150,001 to 250,000: 30 points
- 250,001 to 350,000: 40 points
- above 350,000: 50 points
If you are under RWF 50,000 the card says: 'Sales below 50,000 RWF: 0 points awarded this month.'

question: How do I get orders points?
answer:
Orders points depend on the total value of your paid and confirmed stock orders in the month:
- below RWF 50,000: 0 points
- 50,000 to 100,000: 10 points
- 100,001 to 200,000: 20 points
- 200,001 to 300,000: 25 points
- above 300,000: 30 points
You must have at least RWF 50,000 in orders and at least 2 confirmed paid orders in the month to score. A reinvestment rule can also cap your points (see the 70% rule).

question: What is the 70% reinvestment rule for Orders points?
answer: If your reinvestment rate - how much you reinvest in stock compared with your Outstanding Startup Capital - is below 70%, your Orders points are capped at 20, however large your orders are. The card then shows: 'Orders points capped at 20: reinvestment below 70%.' This is an incentive scoring rule and is separate from the 30% repayment ratio used when vouchers are issued.

question: What are the tiers and quarterly incentive vouchers?
answer:
Your tier depends on your monthly points:
- Platinum (85 to 100 points): RWF 30,000 quarterly voucher
- Gold (70 to 84): RWF 23,000
- Silver (50 to 69): RWF 15,000
- Bronze (below 50): no voucher
The quarterly voucher is only issued if you pass the eligibility conditions.

question: Who qualifies for the quarterly incentive voucher?
answer:
You must meet all three conditions:
1. Your total monthly points are at least 50 in the relevant month.
2. Your phone repayment compliance is at least 80% across the three months of the quarter.
3. There are no confirmed major compliance violations or fraud findings for the period.
If you fail any one of them, there is no voucher for that quarter, even with high points.

question: How will I know my quarterly result?
answer: You receive an SMS at the end of the quarter. If you are eligible it states your tier, points and voucher, for example: 'Congratulations! You are a Gold Agent this quarter: 23,000 RWF voucher issued.' If you are not eligible it states your tier and the reason, for example: 'Your quarterly repayment compliance was below 80%: no voucher issued this quarter.'

question: Where can I see my score and my quarter-to-date progress?
answer: Your dashboard shows three score cards (Repayments, Sales, Orders) with the points earned against the maximum, the numbers used and whether a minimum was missed. It also shows your tier and total points, a quarter-to-date summary with your phone repayment compliance against the 80% threshold and a plain status such as 'On track' or 'At risk: repayment below threshold', and a history of incentive vouchers you received.

question: How can I improve my tier?
answer:
Focus on the three parts of the score:
1. Keep your phone repayment at 100% for the full 20 points (and never below 80% over the quarter to stay eligible).
2. Record every sale in the app and aim for higher monthly sales value - the top 50 points need more than RWF 350,000.
3. Place at least 2 paid orders a month worth more than RWF 300,000 for the full 30 points, and reinvest at least 70% so your Orders points are not capped.
4. Follow program rules - sanctions reduce points or block your voucher.

question: What are sanctions and how do they affect my score?
answer:
Sanctions are applied when program rules are broken, and each one needs a recorded reason:
- Minor non-compliance: minus 5 points
- Moderate non-compliance: minus 15 points and your voucher is held until it is resolved
- Major non-compliance or fraud: you lose the quarterly voucher and the matter is escalated under program rules
You can see the date, level, reason and effect of any sanction in your dashboard, but you cannot edit it.

question: What happens to my repayment score if the phone repayment data is not available?
answer: If IntelliGra's data cannot be retrieved in the scoring window, your repayment score is marked pending, the admin is notified, and the repayment scoring is run manually once the data is available. Your other scores are not affected.

question: Am I scored during a grace period?
answer: No. Agents in a grace period are left out of the monthly scoring.

question: How does the Job Marketplace work for Agents?
answer:
The Job Marketplace (Opportunities tab) shows job listings from verified employers. You can:
- browse by location, pay rate and duration
- save jobs to apply later (saved jobs stay across sessions)
- apply with one tap, using your profile, education and SFH-verified certificates that are filled in for you
- track your applications and read employer feedback
The more certificates and good ratings you have, the better your chances.

question: How do I apply for a job step by step?
answer:
1. Open the Opportunities (Job Marketplace) tab.
2. Browse or filter the jobs and open the one you like.
3. Tap apply - your profile data, education and certificates are filled in automatically.
4. Attach documents if needed, such as your ID card, health certificate or motivation letter (PDF or JPG).
5. Submit. The employer reviews your application.
6. Follow it in My Applications.

question: What do my job application statuses mean?
answer: My Applications shows each application as New, Accepted or Rejected, with a history timeline and direct feedback from the employer (for example 'Congratulations! We have selected you...'). Employers move candidates through New, Shortlisted, Interviewed and then Hired or Rejected. You get push notifications when you are shortlisted, rejected, or when an employer views your application.

question: What is a Fit Score and why can't I see mine?
answer: The Fit Score is a percentage that shows an employer how well your certificates and sales history match a job. It is intentionally visible only to the employer so screening stays professional. What you can see is the employer's feedback and the status of your application.
keywords: why can't i see fit score

question: How are jobs matched to me?
answer: After an employer posts a job, the platform searches the Agent registry for Agents whose certified skills and verified location match. Matching jobs appear in your Opportunities feed. For high-priority roles, the system also pushes recommendations to top-performing Agents with high ratings and certificates. Keeping your certificates current and your profile complete helps you get matched.
keywords: why am i not seeing jobs

question: What happens after I finish a job?
answer: The employer submits a rating and review. It cannot be changed afterwards and it updates your public Reputation Metrics. Strong performance may trigger a tier adjustment that supports your progress from Level A toward Level F.

question: How do employers post and manage jobs?
answer: Employers use a web portal. They create a job from approved templates with a live preview showing exactly how it will look on your phone, then review applicants with Fit Scores and move them through New, Shortlisted, Interviewed and Hired or Rejected. They can message shortlisted talent and are notified of new applicants and expiring posts.

question: What is the message center in the app?
answer: The message center is where you receive announcements, surveys and notices from SFH. Messages are listed newest first with title, date and time, status (pending, delivered, read or failed), channel (app or SMS) and sender. You can filter them, for example to show unread messages. Opening a message marks it read. Messages show in Kinyarwanda or English as sent, and delivered messages can still be read offline. Check the Failed and Pending filters if you expected a message that you cannot see.

question: How do I get help inside the app?
answer:
1. Open the Help (Need Help?) section.
2. Search for your question or browse the categories: Video Tutorials, Inventory, Services, Ikofi and IntelliGra.
3. If you cannot find an answer, tap Ask a Question. This creates a support ticket (in ResolveIt) with your ID, district and the screen you were on.
4. Follow the status of your questions in the app. Outside support hours the app tells you when to expect a reply.
Help content is in Kinyarwanda and English and downloaded content works offline.

question: How do I contact KoraLink support by phone?
answer: Call +250 796 602 807, Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00. When you call, have your name, phone number and the screen where the problem happens ready. For a payment problem, also have the date, time and amount.

question: Is my data safe on KoraLink?
answer:
KoraLink protects your data with:
- Encryption of all personal data at rest and in transit, and HTTPS-only connections
- Token-based (JWT) login and field-level access permissions
- Encrypted PIN storage and PIN protection on wallet transactions
- PCI-DSS Level 4 compliant card handling with card tokenization
- An immutable audit trail of financial, stock and admin actions
- A breach response plan that reports any personal data breach to the NCSA within 48 hours
Never share your PIN or password.

question: What are my data rights under Rwanda's law?
answer: KoraLink follows Rwanda's Law No. 058/2021 on the protection of personal information. The program is registered as a Data Controller with the NCSA and has a Data Protection Officer. You are asked for consent when you register, and you have the right to access your data and to request its erasure. Some financial records (such as sales, commissions and repayments) must be kept for 10 years under RRA rules.

question: How long does KoraLink keep my records?
answer: Financial and fiscal records - sales, commissions, repayments, stock movements and your signing evidence - are kept for 10 years, as required by the Rwanda Revenue Authority. This overrides the Foundation's 7-year minimum.

question: Does the app track my location?
answer: The platform is designed to handle location data using geofencing to monitor Agent activity, and this has privacy considerations that must be respected. Your assigned location (district) is also part of your profile. If you have concerns about location data, ask your SFH supervisor or the Data Protection Officer.

question: Is my sales data used for anything else?
answer: Data created on the platform - your sales performance, transaction history, application scores and stock order volumes - is used to track program performance and to match you with jobs. It can also support micro-loan decisions. Your data is protected under Rwanda's data protection law.

question: Why are all my transactions recorded permanently?
answer: Funders and regulators require full traceability. Every financial, stock, voucher, repayment and administrative action is saved in an audit trail that cannot be edited, so everything can be checked and any dispute can be resolved. It also protects you by showing exactly what happened and when.

question: How do I show that I am unavailable for work or sales?
answer: You can mark yourself as offline/unavailable in the app so supervisors and customers know you are not active. Going unavailable for work or sales may need your supervisor's approval, and supervisors can see your availability status. Tell your supervisor in advance when you will be away.

question: What are the Task Tracker and Work Week Planner?
answer: They are planning tools in the app that help you manage your time, spread your effort across sales, gigs and training, and estimate how much income you can make.

question: How do I make sure all my sales are credited to me?
answer: All consumer sales are unambiguously linked to a single Agent's digital storefront, so 100% of the sales are tracked and attributed to that Agent for commission and inventory. Always record every sale in your own account so your earnings, stock and scores are correct.

question: What is IntelliGra?
answer: IntelliGra is the external system that manages smartphone repayments. KoraLink reads your phone repayment data from it to show your phone repayment status and to calculate your repayment score. KoraLink only reads it and does not own those transactions.

question: What is MVEND?
answer: MVEND is the wallet and payment partner behind your Ikofi wallet. It processes your wallet payments and repayments in real time and supports customer mobile money payments by USSD, STK push or QR code. Wallet actions are protected by your PIN.

question: What is DDIN?
answer: DDIN is the aggregator that provides the digital services you sell in the Services tab - prepaid electricity, MTN and Airtel airtime, RRA tax and Startimes PayTV. Your float is used to pay DDIN when you process a transaction.

question: When does the KoraLink program run?
answer: The program runs under its agreement from 1 March 2025 to 31 August 2029. The Mastercard Foundation evaluates progress in Year 3 to decide on possible expansion. The total program budget is about USD 25,064,916 and is managed by the Foundation.

question: What is the Revolving Fund and why do I repay it?
answer: The Revolving Fund is the program's pool of Repayable Grants. It gives new Agents their starting goods, devices, accessories, digital service float and data. Agents repay what they used, interest-free, and the repaid money is reinvested to support other Agents, so the program can keep helping people beyond the first four years. Repaying on time keeps the fund working for the next Agent.
keywords: why do i have to repay

question: What can I do with USSD on a basic phone?
answer: With the USSD shortcode and SMS confirmations you can register and record sales, check your earnings and fund status, make voluntary repayments, check your Outstanding Startup Capital and Monthly Installment, and place a stock order with the system-determined voucher. Digital service transactions (airtime, electricity, tax, TV) are not available offline.
keywords: what can i do on ussd

question: What is the difference between a voucher and a wallet payment?
answer: A voucher is startup capital from the Revolving Fund that covers part of your stock order and that you repay over time. A wallet payment is the part of the order you pay from your own Ikofi wallet funds. Your order amount always equals Unused Voucher Applied + New Voucher Issued + Wallet Payment.

question: Do vouchers expire?

question: Do I pay both the required repayment and the monthly installment?

question: Where do I go to set up my wallet PIN?
answer:
1. Open :wallet: Wallet. If no PIN has been created, the screen shows PIN Not Set.
2. Tap Set Up PIN.
3. In Enter PIN, type 4 digits. You can use the eye icon to show the digits while typing.

question: How does the two-step Digital Services process work?
answer:
Every DDIN digital service follows the same two-step pattern: Step 1 validates the customer's details; Step 2 executes the transaction.
• MTN Airtime: enter the customer's MTN number and tap Validate Phone; then enter the amount and tap Execute Recharge.
• Airtel Airtime: enter the customer's Airtel number and tap Validate Phone; then enter the amount and tap Execute Recharge.
• Prepaid Electricity: enter the meter number and tap Validate Meter; then enter the amount and tap Execute Transaction and give the customer the token.
• RRA Tax: enter the Doc ID and tap Validate Doc ID; then confirm the amount shown and tap Execute Payment.
• Startimes PayTV: enter the customer's smart-card number; then choose the package and tap Execute Payment.

question: How do I sign my KoraLink agreement in the app?
answer:
To sign your KoraLink agreement (Amasezerano):
1. Go to Profile > Amasezerano (Agreements) and open the agreement under NTARASINYWA (Not yet signed). Check the deadline and agreement number.
2. Read the main agreement and annexes Umugereka 2 and Umugereka 4 before starting.
3. Step 1 — Indangamuntu: enter your national ID number and tap Confirm and continue.
4. Step 2 — Telefoni: verify the registered phone number, request the SMS code, enter the 6-digit code and confirm it.
5. Step 3 — Kwemera amakuru: switch on all three consent statements (I have read the agreement, I understand the obligations, I accept the terms) and tap Continue.
6. Step 4 — Umukono: check your name, draw your signature, use Clear if needed, then tap Save signature.
7. Step 5 — Biometrike: confirm your identity with the fingerprint or Face ID already set up on your phone. If your phone has no biometrics, the guide provides a Continue without biometrics option.
8. Step 6 — Kubaho: take two face photos, check both photos, and confirm them. Use good, even lighting and keep your face clear.
9. Step 7 — Gusinya: switch on the final confirmation that the information is correct and you agree to sign digitally, then tap Sign the agreement.
After signing, the screen shows Agreement signed with a green tick. Tap Download PDF to keep your signed copy; you can also view it later under Profile > Amasezerano.
